hypothesis: E35 (frozen 3 Oct, two seeds, a laptop design read qualitatively) at the protocol's sixteen seeds: a global sign latent leaves the paper's first-order kernel with a bias that data do not remove, and the same kernel on the augmented state (X, G) removes it. Same driver, arms, cells, ladder and reference as E35; only the seed count and the machine change.
design: offsets b in (0, 1, 2), sizes M in (512, 2048), seeds 0-15 (all sixteen run fresh on the cluster, including 0-1), L = 32, rho = 0.85, the registered one-view interface, validation 1024 and test 2048 chains, risk selection over the ladder (10..400), the closed-form two-phase posterior mean as the reference. Arms: em_first_order, em_augmented, lmmse_true, isotropic. Two shards of eight seeds (e35x-s0, e35x-s8), 24 workers each, defq.

predeclared_predictions.P1: At b = 0 augmentation has no systematic cost: the paired mean of log(augmented / first-order) over the sixteen seeds has a 95% bootstrap interval containing 0 at both M. (Replaces E35's 10% band, which two seeds could not hold.)
predeclared_predictions.P2: At b = 2 the first-order arm's deficit is a bias: its seed-mean risk changes by less than 15% from M = 512 to 2048, while the augmented arm's seed-mean risk falls by more than 30% and falls in at least 14 of 16 seeds.
predeclared_predictions.P3: At M = 2048 first-order / augmented exceeds 2 in 16/16 seeds at b = 1 and at b = 2, and its seed mean rises with b over (0, 1, 2); at b = 2 the augmented arm's seed-mean risk is below the linear floor's by a factor of at least 3.
predeclared_predictions.P4: Under the latent the first-order arm is WORSE than the linear floor: first-order / lmmse_true > 1 in 16/16 seeds at b = 1 and b = 2, both M (E35's unregistered observation, 1.5-1.7 at two seeds).

predeclared_analysis: augmented.csv merged over the two shards: per (b, M) the paired per-seed ratios with sixteen seeds; bootstrap intervals by Monte Carlo (200,000 draws, seed 20260912) on the mean of the per-seed log ratio, since 16 seeds cannot be enumerated; at_cap and converged read beside every risk (an augmented arm at cap is an upper bound).
provenance_note: NOT a pre-data registration in the strict sense: E35's two-seed result is frozen and known, and P1 and P4 are written with that knowledge (P1 because E35's band was too tight for two seeds, P4 because E35 showed it unregistered). It is an extension of the seed count on the same driver, cells, arms and analysis; registered before any E35x cell ran.

outcome.P1: FALSIFIED AS WRITTEN, in the favourable direction. The interval does not contain 0 because the augmented arm is LOWER at b = 0: mean log(augmented / first-order) is -0.201 [-0.396, -0.050] at M = 512 and -0.321 [-0.559, -0.083] at M = 2048, i.e. a geometric-mean ratio 0.82 and 0.73, augmented lower in 11 of 16 seeds at both sizes (per-seed ratio 0.26-1.24 at M = 512, 0.25-2.17 at M = 2048). So there is no cost of augmentation, and a modest gain the prediction did not allow for. The verdict does not rest on one seed (dropping any single seed leaves the upper bound at -0.025 or below), and it has the same sign as E35's two-seed means (0.96, 0.89). Both arms are at the checkpoint cap in a few b = 0 cells (first-order 1 and 2 seeds, augmented 2 and 4, at M = 512 and 2048), so the augmented risk is, if anything, an upper bound. The cause is not investigated.
outcome.P2: CONFIRMED. At b = 2 the first-order arm's seed-mean risk changes by +0.2% from M = 512 to 2048 (0.0964 -> 0.0966; predicted: under 15%); the augmented arm's falls by 51.7% (0.0203 -> 0.0098; predicted: over 30%) and falls in 16 of 16 seeds (predicted: at least 14).
outcome.P3: CONFIRMED. At M = 2048 first-order / augmented (seed mean of the per-seed ratios) is 1.55, 7.64, 13.08 at b = 0, 1, 2 (rising), above 2 in 16/16 seeds at b = 1 and at b = 2; at b = 2 the linear floor is 6.3 times the augmented risk (0.0617 / 0.0098; predicted: at least 3). The augmented arm stopped at the last checkpoint in 5 of 16 seeds at b = 1 and in 5 at b = 2 (M = 2048), so its risk is an upper bound there and every ratio is a lower bound.
outcome.P4: CONFIRMED. First-order / linear floor exceeds 1 in 16 of 16 seeds in all four cells: 1.71 (b = 1, M = 512), 1.67 (b = 1, 2048), 1.56 (b = 2, 512), 1.57 (b = 2, 2048); E35's two seeds gave 1.5-1.7.
outcome.unregistered: At b = 0 the linear floor is the exact score (risk 0 to rounding), so ratios to it are undefined there and P4 is read at b > 0 only. One of the 192 EM fits (first-order, b = 0, M = 512, seed 7) has a monotonicity violation of 7.2e-5; every other is below 2e-8 (E35: below 2e-8 throughout); the P1 verdict is unchanged without that seed (interval [-0.400, -0.033]). Seed-mean risks (first / augmented / floor): b = 1: 0.0604 / 0.0207 / 0.0354 (M = 512), 0.0590 / 0.0083 / 0.0354 (M = 2048); b = 2: 0.0964 / 0.0203 / 0.0617, 0.0966 / 0.0098 / 0.0617.
outcome.explained_by: E46 (8 Oct 2026, frozen): the b = 0 gain of the augmented kernel is the reflection symmetry. A first-order kernel fitted on the sequences and their mirror images is 32-39% below the plain first-order fit and 16-17% below the augmented one, and equals a fit on twice as many independent sequences in seed mean.
